correctness.rationale: Use the three local star tetrahedra in integral barycentric coordinates: their sum on each star is the degree, and shared-edge marginals agree. The inverse maps each edge to its 1-marginal; the local parity condition is exactly integrality of the barycentric coordinates. This describes the seven-dimensional lattice and polytope, since matching binary marginals can be coupled across the path. Matching the binary labels of integer lists of local assignments also gives degree-one generation. The facet normals restrict to primitive vanishing-weight coordinates. If both internal edges vary on a face, the projection from the tangent lattice to its zero-weight coordinates is surjective: prescribe those coordinates, use one available center weight to restore the center total, then use available weights of both edge labels independently at each leaf star to match its total and marginal. Hence the active rays extend to a lattice basis. When exactly one internal edge is fixed and the face is maximal with this property, two weights vanish at each adjacent star. Their projections have just the relation that the two missing-label sums agree. Any integer values satisfying this relation extend by restoring the neighboring star totals and the other edge marginal. The resulting four-ray rank-three saturated cone is the unit-square cone; its dual semigroup is nonnegative quadruples with the two pair sums equal, generated by the four cross pairs with one determinant relation. This gives the transverse node ab−cd=0. Smaller faces with a fixed edge are singular by closedness, exhausting the support. Fixing one edge gives a primitive segment times the even-sum lattice tetrahedron, and fixing two gives a product of two primitive segments. These yield the given Segres, total degree 16, and exactly four cross intersections without triples. In positive degrees the monomial basis of the reduced union is the set-union of the component semigroup slices, giving 4(d+1)binom(d+3,3)−4(d+1)^2; at degree zero it has the common unit only. An independent enumeration of compatible star-support patterns confirmed all 711 faces, both dimension vectors and Hilbert values through degree four, adding 600 at that degree.
residual_risks: In characteristic two this is the integral toric model, not a stochastic model obtained by an invertible Fourier transform. Only reduced support and generic component germs are claimed, not the Jacobian scheme or intersection germs.

value.rationale: For the natural next trivalent tree after the four-leaf example, this determines precisely the failure of smoothness in the projective toric compactification. The component and intersection polarizations and complete graded series give usable information not present in the exact model's database row or determined by its ambient dimension and degree. This is more than computing an isolated small face count.
